Tanya — great speaking with you earlier. Short answers up front, then proposed next steps and required artifacts.

Short answers:
- Yes, Redwood will sign a BAA for PHI-bearing workloads. We keep a standard BAA template; happy to send a draft.
- We are SOC 2 Type II. I will ask Laura to extract the relevant controls and provide a one-page summary.
- Encryption: TLS in transit + AES-256 at rest. We support customer-managed keys in Private deployments and Dedicated (depending on config); Hosted API customers can use our KMS integration for managed keys or bring-your-own-key via our enterprise offering.
- Audit logs: accessible via our Console; exportable to S3 / SIEM; retention configurable (default 90 days, options for longer retention on enterprise plans).
- Data residency: we have regions in us-east-1 and us-west-2; Private/VPC can be hosted in your VPC or on-prem.

Hosting tradeoffs (very high level):
- Hosted API: fastest onboarding (days), supports BAA, lower operational overhead, suitable if you can accept Redwood-managed keying or our enterprise KMS integration.
- Dedicated: reserved GPU pools, predictable throughput, can provide stronger isolation and configurable KMS; lead time ~3-6 weeks depending on capacity.
- Private VPC / on-prem: maximum isolation and customer-managed keys; multi-week to multi-month depending on environment and network setup.

Immediate next steps I propose:
1) I will send the following artifacts to you by EOD: SOC2 one-pager, BAA draft, and a short checklist of evidence items.
2) Schedule a 45-minute security deep-dive with Laura (security/compliance) and your security team this week.
3) Aisha will follow up with pricing estimates for Hosted vs Dedicated and an example SOW for Dedicated provisioning.

Do those next steps work? If so, can procurement share a target budget or any hard milestones they need hit for the timeline?

Regards,
Markus Klein
VP, Sales — Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.com

Markus / Aisha / Tanya — attaching the SOC2 one-pager and a short control mapping. High level:

- SOC 2 Type II: Report period 2026-06 through 2027-05 (current). Relevant sections: CC6 (confidentiality), CC7 (availability), CC4 (access controls).
